# Church assets

The saved scene now uses `Sequence/SceneSequence-Church walkthrough.asset` for its single-player demonstration: bells, robin calls, wind, rain, then thunder. The organ and voice bindings remain registered; the sequence does not autostart them. Existing acoustic reflections are retained. See `docs/scene-presentation.md` for the capture workflow and limitations.

All bundled third-party assets below are published under **CC0 1.0**: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/

- **Church model and textures:** Daniel Andersson; explorable-interior adaptation by AnyRPG. https://opengameart.org/content/medieval-church-interior — derived from https://opengameart.org/content/medieval-church . Download: https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/church.blend . Exported to FBX with separate editable parts and centered local origins. Packed textures extracted unchanged. `ChurchCollision.fbx` keeps architectural surfaces and doors, dissolving coplanar detail within 2 degrees; duplicate vertices and degenerate faces are removed. Decorative statue, window bars and small exterior trim are omitted from this approximation. The scene supplies its floor and furniture.
- **Bell recording:** “Church Bell” (0135), Joseph SARDIN / BigSoundBank. https://bigsoundbank.com/church-bell-s0135.html . Original WAV: https://bigsoundbank.com/UPLOAD/bwf-en/0135.wav . `Audio/Bell.wav` preserves the recording, with 60 ms boundary fades, a 0.55 peak and silence to make a 30-second loop. The original contains outdoor ambience and room/environment decay; it is not an anechoic training source.
- **Organ samples:** “Church organ emulation”, FreePats / Roberto, version 2019-09-24, recorded from Fons Adriaensen's Aeolus emulator. https://freepats.zenvoid.org/Organ/pipe-organ.html . Source archive: https://freepats.zenvoid.org/Organ/ChurchOrganEmulation/ChurchOrganEmulation-SFZ-20190924.tar.xz . `Audio/Organ.wav` is an original C / A minor / F / G passage rendered from the nearest supplied note samples, downmixed, resampled and faded, with a 0.45 peak and silence in a 30-second loop. No additional reverb was applied. This is sampled organ emulation, not a recording of a physical church organ or a calibrated acoustic reference.
- **Rain:** “Rain and Thunder #1” (0124), Joseph SARDIN / BigSoundBank. https://bigsoundbank.com/rain-and-storm-s0124.html . Original WAV: https://bigsoundbank.com/UPLOAD/bwf-en/0124.wav . `Audio/RainCourtyard.wav` uses the early 1–13 s excerpt, downmixed to mono, with a one-second constant-power wrap crossfade and a 0.4 peak. The resulting loop is 11 seconds. The original recording's later thunder is not included. The superseded second point-source excerpt, `RainGarden.wav`, remains in checkpoint `0659ec5`.
- **Thunder:** “Thunder #3” (3114), Joseph SARDIN & Axeline T. / BigSoundBank. https://bigsoundbank.com/thunder-3-s3114.html . Original WAV: https://bigsoundbank.com/UPLOAD/bwf-en/3114.wav . `Audio/Thunder.wav` resamples the mono recording from 48 kHz to 44.1 kHz with a polyphase filter, removes its mean, adds 80 ms boundary fades and scales its peak to 0.7. The 11.2-second roll starts at second 8 of a 42-second loop, with silence elsewhere. This is an authored repeating soundtrack, not a stochastic storm simulation.
- **Robin:** “Robin #4” (1670), Joseph SARDIN / BigSoundBank, CC0. https://bigsoundbank.com/robin-4-s1670.html . Original WAV: https://bigsoundbank.com/UPLOAD/bwf-en/1670.wav . `Audio/RobinCall.wav` preserves the 3.115-second recording, resamples to 44.1 kHz, removes its mean, adds 25 ms boundary fades and scales to a 0.6 peak.
- **Tree wind:** “Wind and tree squeaks” (1051), Joseph SARDIN / BigSoundBank, CC0. https://bigsoundbank.com/wind-and-tree-squeaks-s1051.html . Original WAV: https://bigsoundbank.com/UPLOAD/bwf-en/1051.wav . `Audio/TreeWind.wav` uses seconds 20–37, resampled to 44.1 kHz, with a one-second constant-power wrap crossfade, producing a 16-second loop at a 0.4 peak. It includes natural branch creaks; it is not isolated leaf excitation.

`Audio/ThunderCue.wav` prepares the original 3114 recording directly with mean removal, resampling, 30 ms boundary fades and a 0.7 peak. It has no authored eight-second pre-delay. The sequence starts this clip at the visible flash; acoustic transport adds propagation delay. The original recording's own temporal structure and environmental acoustics remain. `BellPresentation.strikes` annotates the existing bell phrase's measured envelope peaks at 0.08, 2.03, 4.02, 6.02, 8.02 and 10.01 seconds. The bell animation is not a vibration simulation.

`Sequence/` contains original mesh/material assets authored by `ChurchSequenceAuthoring`: a hollow bell with a separate clapper and fixed support, a robin with separate wings/beak, and shared tree branch/foliage meshes. The original static `Bell` renderer is hidden; architectural collision and acoustic geometry are preserved. Trees and bird detail are presentation geometry. Static roof heights are sampled from the scene's colliders for visual rain; foliage is not modeled as watertight acoustic or rain shelter.

Textures import as ordinary repeating 3D textures (not the project’s default clamped sprites), capped at 1024 pixels. Both meshes are readable for acoustic compilation and replay. Audio imports as preloaded PCM.

The four authored clip sources play through the existing raytracer. The tower emitter is at the front belfry opening `(0, 52, -4)`, representing radiation out of the tower; it does not model the enclosed bell-to-aperture field. Masonry screens the nave and much of the front courtyard. The east courtyard near `(26, 1, -40)` has a clear path. Weather lives under `Church world / Weather`: one masked rain plane and one elevated thunder point. `RainMask.png` is an original 128 × 192 mask sampled from the scene's static colliders; white marks exposed ground and black covered ground. It imports as readable, linear, uncompressed pixels. `AudioSourcePlane` uses stable spatial samples and cyclic offsets into the one rain clip, with no extra source objects. This approximates outdoor rain ambience, not a vibrating roof, extended lightning channel or calibrated source power. The recordings contain their original environmental acoustics and are scene ambience, not dry acoustic ground truth. Speech remains a separate microphone/remote voice source. Keep the dry `Assets/Audio/church_clap.wav` for isolated acoustic diagnostics; the scene does not automatically play it. Geometry and material coefficients are illustrative and not measured acoustic data.

`Details.fbx` contains original reusable pew, altar, organ, chandelier, window-pane and surrounding-ground meshes made for this scene. `LeadedGlass.png` and `WindowLight.png` are original geometric patterns; `Paving.png` and the wall normal maps derive visual variation from the bundled CC0 stone textures. The normal maps are illustrative relief inferred from texture brightness, not scanned surface measurements. These assets use Unity's existing Standard shader and native lights; there is no new runtime script, shader, post-processing package or lightmap bake. The darker lighting preset uses four candle lights, two window projections and a cool directional light. Flame/glass materials retain their emission keywords after reload.

Pew seat/back collisions use metre-sized boxes on a unit-scale parent, independent of the imported visual node's FBX axis/unit transform. The larger organ has simple wooden housing proxies. Thin closed panes fill selected nave/apse openings and participate in acoustic transport. The surrounding ground has a matching visual/collision/acoustic mesh and joins the courtyard at the same height; its distant edge is hidden by scene fog. Glass/ground acoustic coefficients are illustrative, like the existing stone/wood presets.

Import/export scripts and diagnostic evidence are retained locally under `.context/church-assets/`. No Blender or audio-synthesis dependency is required at runtime.

Weather preparation, source pages/license evidence, download hashes, scene-authoring checks and the silent Unity log are retained in `docs/benchmarks/church-weather-2026-10-22/authoring.zip`. The initially evaluated rain-on-concrete/puddle recordings and Thunder #4 had clipped transients; they are not bundled or used. See `docs/scene-presentation.md` for source positions, verification scope and GPU-memory cost.

## Cathedral room kit

`CathedralRooms.fbx` is original scene geometry authored for this project: pointed arcades and octagonal columns, floor inlays, wall panels, banners, an open baptismal font, jewel panels, reading shelves/books/table/benches, candle stands and timber trusses. Its 13 named parts use the palette in `Assets/Materials/ChurchPresentation/Rooms-*`; the three `Rooms-PBR-*` variants reuse the existing CC0 marble/wood textures. No additional third-party asset license is introduced.

The saved Church scene includes these assets in both visual styles, with physical furniture/structural collision and acoustic proxies. Inlays and small decoration remain visual-only. The table and shelves have ensemble parents so their proxies move with their visuals. The source authoring scripts and validation evidence are archived in `docs/benchmarks/church-rooms-2026-10-22/authoring.zip`; Blender is not a runtime dependency. See `docs/scene-presentation.md` for room views, controls and the scope of verification.

`CathedralAccents.fbx` adds four original decorative mesh parts: nave vault ribs, the sanctuary rose/organ surround, nave sconces, and the reading-chapel crest. It shares the room kit's materials and does not add acoustic/collision geometry. The rose is decorative art, not an additional acoustic window. The original Blender authoring and Unity placement/verification scripts are retained in `docs/benchmarks/church-sources-2026-10-22/authoring.zip`.

### Ground-drop kernel

`Audio/GroundDrop.wav` is original procedural audio generated by `tools/rain_impact.py` (seed 173, 44.1 kHz mono, 24 ms). It is a dry noise impact with zero endpoints and approximately zero DC, not a measured surface response or a sampled rain recording. Source amplitude is normalized by the emission model.
